scope: VERSION29 frozen main paper only; no separate note or earlier revision; 9 keys, every one of 11 citation uses.

uses.source_location: Section 2, pp.70–73, especially Proposition 2.1 and its following construction pp.71–72 (PDF pp.3–6).
uses.support_explanation: Section 2 constructs the initial algebra for a many-sorted signature and identifies each carrier with well-formed expressions of that sort. Its constructor and unique-decomposition discussion supports the raw abstract-syntax attribution. This is ordinary many-sorted syntax, not by itself a treatment of capture avoidance or alpha equivalence. V29 correctly cites separate binding sources and separately assumes initiality stable under parameters in its category D.

uses.source_location: Section 4 “Parchments”, author report pp.15–16 (PDF pp.16–17); Section 4.1 pp.18–19 gives the equational example.
uses.support_explanation: The actual text describes a syntactic signature whose sorts include terms and sentences, with constructors for those sorts and the language as the initial algebra. It describes the signature-indexed Lang functor and points to first-order, equational and Horn logic. This exactly supports the stated attribution; it does not supply v29’s internal, parameter-stable construction. The full primary author report was read; publisher metadata independently identifies the 1986 chapter. The report has different pagination from the published pp.313–333, but the cited section number agrees.

uses.source_location: Sections 2–4, PDF pp.4–9: Theorem 2.1; Section 3 “Substitution”; Theorems 4.1–4.2.
uses.support_explanation: Section 2 represents binding signatures on covariant presheaves and characterizes terms modulo alpha equivalence as the free signature algebra on variables. Section 3 develops single and simultaneous substitution; Section 4 characterizes the compatible algebra-plus-substitution model by initiality. The article’s terms are alpha classes/canonical nameless implementations, as v29 says. Its hypotheses and setting are not those of an arbitrary category D; v29 uses this as background and explicitly distinguishes its raw named syntax and admissibility subobject.

uses.source_location: Section 6, full author text pp.13–20: initial-algebra property (54), Theorem 6.2, Theorem 6.5, Corollary 6.7, Example 6.9.
uses.support_explanation: Section 6 builds inductive FM-sets using atom abstraction, identifies the lambda syntax with alpha classes, obtains iteration/recursion from initiality, and constructs capture-avoiding substitution in Example 6.9. The setting requires finite support and freshness restrictions; v29 does not directly invoke that theorem for its category D and accurately distinguishes its raw named syntax.

uses.source_location: Section 2, Example 1(3), author PDF p.4; preceding typed-binding definition and immediately following initial-algebra characterization.
uses.support_explanation: Example 1(3) gives the typed binding signature for first-order classical logic, including an existential quantifier, negation and disjunction. The preceding paragraph explicitly identifies alpha-equivalent terms, and the following paragraph characterizes syntax as an initial algebra in the category of presentation models. The cited claim says only “a quantifier”, so existential rather than universal causes no mismatch. The typed presheaf setting is not silently imported as a theorem about v29’s category D.

uses.source_location: Proof of Corollary 6.7, full author text p.17 (PDF p.17).
uses.support_explanation: The proof replaces X by Lambda_alpha × X, applies initial-algebra iteration, and uses uniqueness to show the first projection recovers the original term. This is exactly the product-carrier trick being compared in v29. The source’s additional freshness condition is required for its binding theorem; the comparison borrows only this general recursion-from-iteration argument, with v29’s own explicitly defined slice algebra.

uses.source_location: p.742 Proposition1.1.4 (PDFp4); pp747–748 Definitions1.4.3–1.4.4 and Proposition1.4.5 (PDFpp9–10)
uses.support_explanation: Proposition1.1.4 characterizes the least rule-closed set by finite-length proofs for a finitary rule set. Proposition1.4.5 gives the well-founded proof-tree characterization; the preceding p747 discussion observes that finitary proof trees are finite. V29 expressly assumes a finite maximum arity N and presents the following slice-category construction as its own reformulation, so it does not falsely attribute that internal categorical generalization to Aczel.
uses.required_correction: None. Optional improve locator by adding pp.742,747–748.

uses.source_location: Lemma 3.6, p.31:10; proof p.31:11 (PDF pp.10–11), following coalgebra Lemma 3.3.
uses.support_explanation: Lemma 3.6 states exactly that an (E,M) factorization system lifts to algebras for an endofunctor preserving E. In v29 the base is the regular slice D/F, with regular epimorphisms and monomorphisms. H preserves the left class by regular-epi stability under finite products/pullbacks and preservation of coequalizers by finite coproducts. The conclusion map is an H-algebra map to the terminal slice algebra, so factoring it is a valid instance. V29 supplies its own least-subobject proof rather than attributing that whole theorem to this lemma.

uses.source_location: Preliminaries(a), numbered paragraph0.10, p7 (publisher excerpt PDFp3)
uses.support_explanation: All three displayed propositional schemata in v29 match the three propositional axioms in 0.10 exactly, after replacing source implication notation. HP uses a conditional quantifier rule and treats equality as special axioms in0.11, but v29 attributes only the three propositional schemata to HP.
uses.required_correction: No substantive correction. Prefer “0.10, p.7” over “Section0.10” because 0.10 is a numbered paragraph.

uses.support_explanation: Axioms4–5 exactly match universal instantiation and the displayed distribution axiom. §2.11 defines the free-for condition. V29 enforces the first restriction through Adm and the second through x absent from FV(phi). Source generalization is unrestricted for theorem proofs; v29 also restricts nonlogical axioms to sentences, so its generalization rule introduces no omitted open-assumption restriction.

The source gives universally quantified variable reflexivity and variable substitutivity, subject to free-for capture avoidance. It also illustrates replacing a variable by the constant2. V29 uses the corresponding all-term reflexivity and all-term formula-substitution schemata, with both substitutions admissible. The citation supports the stated equality principles; it does not literally print the exact term-parametrized schemata.
uses.required_correction: Optional precision: say “We use the term-instantiated form of the reflexivity and substitutivity principles in §3.1” or add a brief derivation. Do not call the displayed term schemata verbatim Hirst–Hirst axioms.
